_about: Vendor sources that state, per release line of a product, whether a CVE affects the line (the feeds module's line sources), and how each is read. sources: source (the built-in feed id), name (how findings name the source in a sentence), products (catalogue product ids the source speaks for), listed (what a row states: semver_range = a vulnerable and a patched semver range per release line; last_affected = the newest affected release of each line, every earlier release of the line affected too), absent (what a release line the source does not list for a CVE it covers means: unaffected_if_supported = not affected when the vendor supported the line on the day the CVE was published, by the product's line support; unaffected_if_assessed = not affected when the document that lists the CVE assesses the line (has a release of it in its product list) and lists none of its releases as affected, while the source is fresh and the document is not older than the CVE; unknown = nothing), ref (where the vendor describes the data), builds (the distributions of the product whose releases the source numbers: a release past the newest affected one is fixed only for them; for another build, or one not named, it decides nothing), csaf (catalogue product id: how a CSAF document names it: cpe, the NVD part:vendor:product of its products; branch, the product tree branch its products are under when they carry no CPE, as "<branch> Version <release>" or "<branch> Version <branch>:<release>"; other, lower-case texts that mark another edition of the product in a release's name or CPE, whose releases are not the product's). A source with listed last_affected reads CSAF documents and needs a csaf entry for each product. support: sources of line support only (release, end of support), never of a CVE verdict: source (the built-in feed id) and products (catalogue product id: the product's name at that source). Read by modules/feeds and checked by its tests; a vendor's convention is data, never code.
